Twelve speakers, listed by surname

Every name, description and session on this page is invented for the template. Nobody listed here is a real person, and no biography here describes real work. One name, Ruth Pellamy, links through to the example talk page.

  • Neve Ashlock

    Chairs rooms. Opens the congress and holds all three assemblies.

    • Fri 09:30Opening the doors
    • Fri 16:30Assembly: what the first day left open
    • Sat 16:45Assembly: the long list
    • Sun 14:00Closing assembly

  • Kwesi Barrowman

    Works on procurement and the long tail of parts that are no longer made.

    • Fri 11:00The cost of a spare part
    • Sat 13:30Two hundred years of pipe

  • Lior Fenwick

    Holds open tables. Writes down what was said and circulates it the next morning.

    • Fri 10:15Open table: what broke this year
    • Sat 11:30Open table: small repairs
    • Sun 13:00The last mile is a stair

  • Dmitri Halloran-Fisk

    Takes things apart in front of people and puts most of them back together.

    • Fri 15:30Taking a pump apart
    • Sat 09:30Soldering for people who drop things
    • Sun 10:00Repair table, with your own broken thing

  • Ode Kirchmeyer

    Interested in forms, paper trails and the protocols that survive a power cut.

    • Sat 10:30Paper is a protocol
    • Sun 11:00Open table: what we should have said

  • Ruth Pellamy

    Works on registers, rotas and handover notes, and argues that these are the documents worth publishing.

    • Fri 10:00Maintenance as a public act
    • Sun 10:00Sunday, and the work continues

  • Marisol Pentreath

    Draws plans and writes reports for people who were not in the room.

    • Fri 13:15Drawing a plan a stranger can read
    • Sat 13:30Writing a fault report somebody reads
    • Sun 13:00Packing the hall down

  • Tomas Quilley

    Reads meters, and is suspicious of anything that counts by itself.

    • Fri 10:00Reading a meter by hand
    • Sat 11:30Counting what the meter misses

  • Solveig Rannoch

    Keeps archives and budgets, and believes both should be readable aloud.

    • Fri 15:30The long afternoon of a public database
    • Sat 10:30The archive in the basement
    • Sun 11:00A budget you can read aloud

  • Imri Sandoval-Roe

    Works on registers and maps, and on who is allowed to change them.

    • Fri 14:15A register nobody can edit
    • Sat 15:45The map and the ledger

  • Bea Tornquist

    Studies queues, rotas and the hours nobody wants to be awake for.

    • Fri 13:15Who is on call at three in the morning
    • Sat 09:30What a queue knows

  • Asta Vennemo

    Loses maps professionally, then writes about how it happened.

    • Fri 11:15Nine ways to lose a map
    • Sat 14:30Handing over the keys
